tui.transcript.ask.key_name.note: The ask card's Q&A row for a SECRET answer: only the collected key NAMES are shown, never values. The suffix disambiguates `[DEPLOY_KEY]` from the secret it stands in for (design round 1, D11) — keep it a short parenthetical, not a sentence.

tui.transcript.ask.not_answered.note: The ask card's Q&A row when a non-secret question went unanswered (timeout or a declined prompt). Distinct from 'not provided', which is about a secret's key never being collected.

tui.transcript.ask.not_provided.note: The ask card's Q&A row when a secret question's key was never provided. Distinct from 'not answered' (a non-secret question); the two must not collapse to one word, they name different states.

tui.transcript.attach.receipt.note: The receipt row under a prompt with pasted attachments: the app confirming BYTES were attached, not repeating the pasted marker (which the user could have typed). ICU plural; the leading arrow is the receipt mark and is part of the value.

tui.transcript.catchup.headline.note: The wake catch-up receipt's headline. `{label}` is the rendered missed-wakes count (see catchup.missed); the em dash joins them in ONE line by design. 'catch-up' is the wake system's own term — keep it short, it rides a one-row receipt.

tui.transcript.catchup.missed.note: The missed-wakes count that fills catchup.headline's `{label}`. ICU plural. Rides a one-row receipt on the transcript spine; 'wake' is the product term for a scheduled session wake.

tui.transcript.queued.newest.note: The marker on the NEWEST queued prompt: a state plus an OFFER ('esc takes it back'), and the offer can be refused — the refusal has its own sentence. The leading middle dot is the marker and part of the value. Only the newest queued message offers recall, so this key must stay longer than queued.older by exactly that clause.

tui.transcript.queued.older.note: The same state WITHOUT the recall offer, for every queued message but the newest: a second row advertising the same key would promise a recall the press declines (UX round 2, U4). Deliberately a strict prefix of queued.newest's words.

tui.transcript.sender.pid.note: One identity bit on a peer message's sender line: the process id that sent it. Composed into a ' · '-joined line with the name and model, so keep it to the label and the number.

tui.transcript.sender.unknown.note: The sender fallback when nothing identifies the peer. MUST stay the same vocabulary harness/comms.py uses for the same case: a reader meeting one in a transcript and one in a tool result must not read them as different states.
